At 10:30 a.m. 3/6/38, information was received by
the undersigned regarding a raid which was carried out by a
party of Japanese on a private radio station, situated at Lane
No. 429, House No. 80, Race Course Road, at approx. 5 a.m. today.

1. Four ordinary code books.

2. One secret code book of the Ministry of Railways.

the construction of a radio set as well as diary
written by some person relating to personal affairs.

note addressed by Chang Chi Yung (張季雍) to

of Communications, asking permission to continue to
draw $60.00 per mensem instead of $50.00 on the ground
that the living expenses in Shanghai have been greatly
increased recently. The writer also pointed out that
he was working in very dangerous circumstances and that
he would be killed should his activities be detected by
the "enemy."

accounts and miscellaneous notes.

At 10.33.a.m. 5-6-38, a telephone message was received from C.P.C. 2318 over Street Tel. Box No. 6, reporting that Japanese were visiting the radio station at 40/429 Race Course Road.

S.I. Moffat, C.D.S. 6 and the undersigned immediately attended the scene and ascertained that a party consisting of Sergt. Major Sakamoto rep: of Japanese Military Authorities in plain clothes and three male Chinese had arrived at the above address at 10.30.a.m. 5-6-38 in a motor car bearing number plate 37152 (Not S.M.C.)

Enquiries ascertained that they had come to see that the radio station was correctly sealed and after asking the chief tenant Chen Hsin Yue (陈心耕) a few questions as to rent and length of tenancy of the sub-tenants, who occupied the radio station, the party left the premises at 10.50.a.m. 5-6-38. No seals were broken and nothing was disturbed.

Inspector Everest attended the premises as the Japanese party were leaving.

Military Authorities.

At 11.15a.m. 3-6-38, D.I. Glover telephoned D.I.
Hill stating that information had been received to the
effect that a party of Japanese had apprehended two
Chinese at House 80 Lane 429 Racecourse Road.

On the instruction of D.I. Hill the undersigned
D.S.I. Tsai Liu and C.D.3. 66 proceeded to Racecourse
Road but failed to locate No. 80 Lane 429 Racecourse
Road. The highest No. in Lane 429 is 66.

Immediate communication was made with D.I. Glover
who when acquainted with the foregoing discovered from
D.3.I. Chu Shou Ling that an error had been made and that
the proper number in Lane 429 was 40 not 80.

On receipt of this information a visit was
immediately paid to No. 40 and on the third floor in a
flat, consisting of three rooms a kitchen and bathroom
it was established that plain clothes Japanese and three
male Chinese had visited the premises at 8a.m. 3-6-38 and
remained thereon for 40 minutes conversing with one
Tsang Kyien Yoong (張季雄), alias Tsang Pei Jih (張培傑)
age 30, Kiangsu, a wireless operator. Last mentioned
from Chen Hsin Yue (陳心耕), chief tenant it was
ascertained had rented the premises at $75.00 per month

报告日本军方当局非法行动。

1938年6月3日上午11时15分，Glover 副总督察致电 Hill 副总督察，称收到情报，指一群日本人在跑马厅路 429 弄 80 号逮捕了两名中国人。

根据 Hill 副总督察的指示，下述人员、侦探副督察蔡刘和刑事侦缉处 3 科 66 号警员前往跑马厅路，但未能找到跑马厅路 429 弄 80 号。429 弄的最大门牌号为 66 号。

随即与 Glover 副总督察取得联系，他在获悉上述情况后，从第三区副督察周守灵处发现出现错误，429 弄的正确门牌号是 40 号而非 80 号。

收到此信息后，立即访问了 40 号，在三楼的一套由三个房间、一个厨房和一个浴室组成的公寓内，查明便衣日本人和三名中国男子于1938年6月3日上午8时访问了该处所，并停留了40分钟，与无线电台操作员张季雄（别名张培杰），30岁，江苏人交谈。据主要承租人陈心耕证实，最后提到的此人于

in January 1938 and installed a wireless transmitter and
receiving set stating it was a legally registered Radio
Station. He had rented the premises together with one
Wong Tse Dah (王士達), 30, Cangzoh, also a wireless
operator.

The above information was obtained from the chief
tenant, and one Yih Kwang Ling (葉光林), 24, Chekiang,
a tea boy employed by the wireless operator.

During the visit by the Japanese and his three
Chinese companions the tea-boy and Wong Tse Dah were not
allowed in the wireless room where a conversation took
place between the Japanese, his companions and Tsang
Kyien Yoong.

Whilst the conversation was taking place Wong Tse
Dah left the premises.

The conversation lasted for approximately 40
minutes after which the Japanese and his three Chinese
companions left the premises.

Soon after they left Tsang Kyien Yoong also left
and told the tea-boy to take special care of everything
until he returned. This was all ascertained on the arri-
val of the undersigned and detectives aforementioned. It
was further elicited that the Japanese intended to return
and that they had left a Chinese agent as guard in the
pages.zh:
1/2.

1938年1月以每月 75.00 美元的价格租下该处所，并安装了无线电发射机和接收机，声称这是一个合法注册的无线电台。他与另一名无线电台操作员王士达，30岁，常州人，共同租下了该处所。

上述信息是从主要承租人和受雇于无线电台操作员的茶役叶光林，24岁，浙江人处获得的。

在日本人及其三名中国同伴访问期间，茶役和王士达不被允许进入无线电台室，日本人与其同伴及张季雄在该室内进行了谈话。

谈话进行时，王士达离开了该处所。

谈话持续了约 40 分钟，随后日本人及其三名中国同伴离开了该处所。

他们离开后不久，张季雄也离开了，并告诉茶役在他回来之前要特别小心照看一切。这是下述人员和前述侦探到达后查明的全部情况。进一步获悉，日本人打算返回，并且留下了一名中国特工作为看守在

pages.en:
1/3.

room adjoining the wireless room.
He was located on the verandah and gave his name
as Ho Sung Pao ( 華春浦 ), 40, Shantung, ex-private
watchman.
D.I. Hill was informed immediately and he in turn
informed Inspector Everest who communicated full parti-
culars to Mr. Robertson, D.C."A".
Mr. Robertson, then instructed Inspector Everest
to inform the American Marine Headquarters.
Shortly after this, D.I. Hill, D.S. Wilkinson,
and D.S. Kobayashi (the latter being called by D.I.Hill)
came to No. 40 just behind the a plain clothes Japanese
and two male Chinese as follows:- Sergeant Major Saim-
moto of the Japanese Military Water Police Headquarters
on the Floating Restaurant, Peking Road Jetty and two
agents Ang Pau San ( 杭參十 ), 36, Shantung, and one
Tsang Kwei San ( 張官山 ), 32 Shantung.
The sergeant major was at this time informed
through D.S. Kobayashi that his procedure was out of
order. He replied that he was aware of this, but
circumstances had prevented him from carrying out the
proper procedure, because he had information that a
private wireless station in premises No. 40/42 Racecourse
Road was communicating in code with Chinese Military in
pages.zh:
1/3.

与无线电室相邻的房间。
他在游廊上被发现，自报姓名为 Ho Sung Pao（華春浦），40岁，山东人，前私人巡夜员。
立即通知了侦探督察 Hill，他随即通知了督察 Everest，后者将详细情况通报给“A”区副总监 Robertson 先生。
Robertson 先生随后指示督察 Everest 通知美国海军陆战队司令部。
此后不久，侦探督察 Hill、侦探警佐 Wilkinson 和侦探警佐 Kobayashi（后者由侦探督察 Hill 叫来）来到跑马厅路40号，紧随其后的是一名便衣日本人和两名中国男子，具体如下：日本海军宪兵队驻北京路码头浮式餐厅的军曹长 Saimmoto，以及两名特工 Ang Pau San（杭參十），36岁，山东人，和 Tsang Kwei San（張官山），32岁，山东人。
此时，通过侦探警佐 Kobayashi 告知该军曹长，其行事程序不合规矩。他回答说他知道这一点，但情况使他无法执行正当程序，因为他获悉跑马厅路40/42号 premises 内的一处私人无线电台正以密码与中国军方在

pages.en:
1/4.

Hankow, therefore he had only visited the premises with
a view to bribing the wireless operator to disclose the
code and information.

He further stated that Tsang Kien Yeong after slight
persuasion had agreed to accept $100.00 and co-operate
with the Japanese Military.

After this promise the Sergeant Major and his three
accomplices left the premises and proceeded in their
way to Japanese Military Water Police Headquarters to
notify the officer in charge the result of their
investigations.

Whilst on their way to Headquarters the Sergeant
Major suddenly thought it would be advisable to post
an agent on the premises. He immediately detailed Vee
Sung Pao to return and prevent Tseng Kyien Yeong from
leaving the premises. However he arrived too late, Tseng
Kyien Yeong having already decamped.

The Sergeant Major was informed at this juncture
that agents acting in this manner would be taken to the
station and interrogated also that should an arrest take
place, the person arrested must be taken to the station
and questioned after which handing over would take place
should the necessary permission be granted by Headquarters.
He was further informed that nothing could be taken away
pages.zh:
1/4.

汉口进行通讯，因此他访问该处所只是为了贿赂无线电操作员以获取密码和信息。

他还进一步陈述说，经稍加劝说，Tsang Kien Yeong 已同意接受100.00美元并与日军合作。

做出此承诺后，军曹长及其三名同伙离开了该处所，前往日本海军宪兵队司令部，向负责官员通报其调查结果。

在前往司令部的途中，军曹长突然认为在该处所部署一名特工是明智之举。他立即指派 Vee Sung Pao 返回，以防止 Tseng Kyien Yeong 离开该处所。然而他到达得太晚了，Tseng Kyien Yeong 已经逃跑。

在此关头，有人告知军曹长，以此种方式行事的特工将被带到警局接受讯问；此外，如果发生逮捕，被捕者必须被带到警局进行讯问，之后若总部批准必要的许可，方可移交。他还被告知，根据

pages.en:
1/5.

as per joint instructions of Mr. Robertson, D.O."A"
and Mr. Asire, D.D.O."A".

One of the agents left the premises at this time
and communicated with Japanese Military Headquarters
resulting in the officer in charge Capt. Yoshida
coming to 40/429 Racecourse Road where on being
acquainted with the procedure necessary and the situation
as it stood at that time requested that the premises be
searched.

The request was granted and a thorough search
made of the wireless room two bedrooms, a kitchen and
bathroom where various papers and documents referring to
the recent occupiers were discovered and parcelled to-
gether.

The Japanese Officer was then informed that the
S.M.P. would take charge of the premises etc and place
a guard over same pending negotiations with Police
Headquarters as to disposal of the documents, and the
tea-boy. A guard was then placed on the premises. The
Japanese Officer assented and left for police headquarters.
At this time a message was received at the station from
Marine Headquarters requesting information. A reply was
given to the effect that the Japanese had left.

Later in the afternoon, Capt. Yoshida came to
pages.zh:
1/5.

“A”区行动主任 Robertson 先生和“A”区副行动主任 Asire 先生的联合指令，不得带走任何物品。

此时，其中一名特工离开该处所并与日本军方司令部取得联系，导致负责军官 Yoshida 上尉来到跑马厅路40/429号，在了解必要程序和当时的局势后，请求对该处所进行搜索。

该请求获准，对无线电室、两间卧室、一间厨房和浴室进行了彻底搜查，发现了涉及近期居住者的各种纸张和文件，并将其打包在一起。

随后告知该日本军官，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）将接管该处所等，并安排警卫看守，以待与警察总部就文件处置及茶役问题进行的谈判。随后在该处所部署了一名警卫。该日本军官表示同意，并前往警察总部。此时，警局收到来自海军陆战队司令部的消息，询问情况。回复称日本人已经离开。

当天下午晚些时候，Yoshida 上尉来到

pages.en:
1/6.

this station with D.S.I. Umemoto and D.S. Uruma of the
Special Political Office, S.M.P. Headquarters to
again view premises 40/429 Racecourse Road.

They were accompanied by D.I.Hill, the undersigned,
and D.J. Kobayashi, when a final search of the premises
was made. At this time Capt. Yoshioka stated that the
transmitting set and receiving set would possibly be
confiscated by his superior command and requested the
S.M.P. enquire as to its origin and owner-ship. The
entire Japanese party with the exception of D.S.Kobayashi
then left the premises whilst they were sealed and
locked pending further negotiations.

A J.P.C. and C.P.C. were posted on guard and
will remain so in shifts until a definite decision
has been made as to the wireless operators documents
and tea-boy. Previous to the second visit by the
Japanese Military, Inspector Everest visited the premises
with S.I. Moffat.

Enquiries re the origin of the wireless apparatus
a 200 Watts "Mac" transmitter, Serial No. 1820 revealed
that it had been sold by the Leeds Engineering Corporation
Weihaiwei Road for $1348.00 on October 5th 1937 to one
F.L. Huang a representative of the Nanking Government.
The apparatus had been taken away personally by
pages.zh:
1/6.

本警局，随行的有上海公共租界工部局警务处总部特别政治科的副侦探督察 Umemoto 和侦探警佐 Uruma，再次查看跑马厅路40/429号的处所。

陪同他们的有侦探督察 Hill、签署人以及侦探警佐 Kobayashi，当时对该处所进行了最后搜查。此时，Yoshioka 上尉（原文如此，前文为 Yoshida）表示，发射机和接收机可能会被其上级指挥部没收，并要求上海公共租界工部局警务处查询其来源和所有权。除侦探警佐 Kobayashi 外，全体日本人员随后离开该处所，该处所被封存并上锁，以待进一步谈判。

部署了一名日本巡捕和中国巡捕进行看守，并将轮班值守，直到对无线电操作员的文件和茶役做出明确决定为止。在日本军方第二次来访之前，Everest 督察曾与副督察 Moffat 一起访问过该处所。

关于无线电设备起源的调查，一台200瓦“Mac”发射机，序列号1820，显示该设备于1937年10月5日以1348.00美元的价格由威海卫路的 Leeds Engineering Corporation 出售给南京政府代表 F.L. Huang。该设备由

The tea-boy brought to the station knew nothing
about the wireless having been employed subsequent to its
installation. (Statement attached).
At the request of the Japanese Authorities and
on instructions of Mr. Aeirs D.D.O."A" he has been detained
in the Finger Print room until 9a.m. 4-6-38 when further

The documents will be forwarded to Headquarters

Chengtu Rd. Stn    3-8-38    xxxxxx    Clerk Tan.

Formerly I was a hawker in the country and in April last
year, I proceeded to Woo Lih Che, Anhwei Province, where I
joined the Nanking-Kiangsu Railway Station as a tenboy. Through
my occupation, I met one Lee Wai Zah who was a clerk of the
above railway station. The above railway station stopped
functioning in August 1937, when the Sino-Japanese Hostilities
broke out. At that time, Lee Wai Zah received a letter from
his wife, which stated that Soochow was no longer a safe place
and that she had evacuated to Shanghai with her neighbours,
taking up residence at 113A North Honan Road. Lee Wai Zah
then decided to come to Shanghai and I, upon knowing this,
asked him to take me with him and he agreed. We both arrived
here on 27-8-37 and I stayed at his home at the above mentioned
address. I did not seek for any position at that time, because
I had some money in my pocket but on the other hand, I asked
Lee to try and find employment for me. In February, this year,
Lee introduced me to a radio station of the Board of Communica-
tion, Central Government (40 Morris Terrace, Chungking Road) as
a tenboy and I was allowed to draw $18.00 per month. According
to Lee, his friend Tsang Chi Yeong also worked at this radio
station, his capacity being a wireless operator. He stated
that his friend Tsang Chi Yeong changed duty with another
wireless operator named Wang Tse Dah, each on duty on every
2nd day. The chief of the radio station was one named Yue Tung
Shing whom I met once when I first went there. In March this
year, Yue proceeded to Hongkong and the radio station was left
in charge of Tsang Chi Yeong. When I went to the wireless room,
pages.zh:
Yih Kwang Ling，24岁，男茶役，住重庆路 Morris Terrace 40号。
S.D.C. 98
浙江
译文
成都路警局    1938年8月3日    xxxxxx    书记员 Tan。

以前我在乡下做小贩，去年四月，我前往安徽省芜湖，在那里加入了宁沪铁路局车站担任茶役。通过我的工作，我结识了 Lee Wai Zah，他是上述车站的一名职员。1937年8月中日敌对行动爆发时，上述车站停止运作。当时，Lee Wai Zah 收到妻子的一封信，信中说苏州不再安全，她已与邻居撤离到上海，居住在河南北路113A号。Lee Wai Zah 随后决定来上海，我得知此事后，请他带我同行，他同意了。我们两人于1937年8月27日抵达此处，我住在他上述地址的家中。当时我没有寻找任何职位，因为我身上有些钱，但另一方面，我请 Lee 试着为我找份工作。今年二月，Lee 将我介绍到中央政府交通部的一处无线电台（重庆路 Morris Terrace 40号）担任茶役，我每月可领取18.00美元。据 Lee 说，他的朋友 Tsang Chi Yeong 也在这家无线电台工作，职务是无线电操作员。他说他的朋友 Tsang Chi Yeong 与另一位名叫 Wang Tse Dah 的无线电操作员轮流值班，每两天值一次班。无线电台的负责人名叫 Yue Tung Shing，我第一次去那里时见过他一面。今年三月，Yue 前往香港，无线电台由 Tsang Chi Yeong 负责。当我去无线电室时，

pages.en:
- 2 -

I sometimes saw Tsang Chi Yoong wearing a pair of receivers
at his ears and jotting down notes with a pen. I do not know
what he wrote about, because I have no such kind of knowledge
and furthermore I never asked him about it and, due to this,
I never knew anything about the radio station. At 8 a.m.
this morning, Tsang Chi Yoong was in the wireless room, when
a Japanese appeared and, in the wireless room, Tsang talked
to 3 Chinese who were brought there by the Japanese. About
half an hour later, the party left the radio station. Tsang
Chi Yoong later also left the radio station telling me that
he would be back pretty soon and simultaneously instructing me
not to leave, but he never came back again. About 20 minutes
later, a male Chinese wearing black Cantonese jacket and pants
who had visited the radio station with the party this morning
appeared again when he kept the station under observation. At
11 a.m. the Police attended and they brought me to the Chengtu
Road Station.

The above is my true statement.

〔此处为签名〕
Signed and crossmarked.

我有时看到 Tsang Chi Yoong 耳朵上戴着耳机，用笔做笔记。我不知道他写的是什么，因为我没有这方面的知识，而且我也从未问过他，因此，我对无线电台的情况一无所知。今天早上8点，Tsang Chi Yoong 正在无线电室，这时出现了一个日本人，在无线电室里，Tsang 与日本人带来的3名中国人交谈。大约半小时后，这群人离开了无线电台。Tsang Chi Yoong 后来也离开了无线电台，告诉我他很快就会回来，同时指示我不要离开，但他再也没有回来。大约20分钟后，今天早上随那群人访问过无线电台的一名身穿黑色粤式夹克和裤子的中国男子再次出现，他对电台进行了监视。上午11点，警察赶到，他们把我带到了成都路警局。

以上是我的真实陈述。

〔此处为签名〕
签名并画押。
